Overnight the euro slipped from 1.09748 to 1.09575 and is now back on today's open price, 1.09609. Just under the Asia low there is a 4-hour zone where buyers stepped in before.

London often opens with one push lower to trigger the stops under the Asia low, then turns. We wait for a 5-minute candle to close back above 1.09575. If the euro closes a 15-minute candle below 1.09540 instead, we stand aside. It is a US holiday, so moves may be small and slow.

In plain English

Between 07:00 and 09:25 the euro climbed from 1.09643 to 1.09819, through the overnight high. It is now easing back to 1.09709.

When a morning move is strong, the next good buy is usually on the way back down, around two-thirds of the way into the move. That is 1.09695. If price falls back under the morning low, the move has failed and we step aside.

The trader's view

  • Dollar: synthetic DXY fell from 103.797 (07:00) to 103.664 (09:25), through its Asia low 103.682, and is back at 103.758, still under its open 103.806.
  • Pair: euro still the stronger (STRENGTH EUR +0.08% · GBP +0.03%, EUR/GBP 0.83687 above its open). GBP/USD took its Asia high by 1.2 pips (1.31204) and slipped back: the weaker pair.
  • News: none confirmed in the window; US Thanksgiving, thin afternoon.

ICT breakdown

12:00Review
London review

No dip, then a breakeven pullback buy

London never gave the 06:40 dip: the euro's low was 1.09643 at 07:00, 7 pips above the Asia low, and it ran straight up through the Asia high to 1.09819 at 09:25. The 10:00 call bought the pullback at 1.09695 (filled 10:10), reached 1.09770 at 10:40 (+7.5 pips), moved the stop to entry and was taken out at entry at 11:25.

What to learn from this All levels

What to learn: on a thin holiday morning the euro skipped the dip and ran first. When London expands in the week's direction without a raid, the trade is the pullback, and a 17-pip London range leaves little for a 12-pip target.

ICT note: Asia high BSL 1.09748 taken as a run, not a sweep; the dollar ran its Asia low SSL 103.682 into the weekly bull IFVG 103.639-103.789 and bounced, which capped the euro's second leg.

In plain English

London pushed the euro up from 1.09643 to 1.09819, then it slipped back to 1.09692. Today's open price, 1.09609, sits just under the London low.

A common afternoon move is a quick dip under the morning's low to shake out buyers, then a return. We only buy if a 5-minute candle closes back above 1.09643. With the US on holiday, the move may never come: then we do nothing.
